title: 抽样率与放大口径

definition.pairing: same bikeid, consecutive observed trips inside the window, next start after current start; cross-day pairs kept; userid not required
definition.distance: haversine between decoded geohash cell centroids of trip k end and trip k+1 start (m)
definition.bands: exact = same geohash string; le160 = <=160 m; le250 = <=250 m; inclusive

ratios.conclusion: A (10-19 May, bbox, consecutive observed trips inside the window, cross-day kept, userid not required, decoded cell-centroid haversine) reproduces 12.83/17.72/19.97%. Requiring same userid gives 58.1/75.1/80.9%; same-day only gives 26.5/35.8/39.5%; all 14 days give 11.9/16.4/18.5%.

p_estimate.model: a_250 is set to 1; a_d below 1 measures geohash/GPS jitter. a values must lie in [0,1].  Placebo pairs (k,k+2) and (k,k+3) are definitely moved, so b_d from them approximates the false-match rate; the two legs make them slightly conservative (too large) as a null for exactly one missed order.
p_estimate.why_not_unique: only m_d is observed; p, a_d and b_d are not separately identified without the a_250=1 and placebo-null assumptions. Different (p, jitter) pairs can reproduce the same three bands.

resample.verdict: not reproducible as a general statement. Seed 0 reproduces the paper's 338,401/330,586/334,436/335,642 (all within 4%), but across 200 thinnings the q=5% distribution has 5th-95th percentile 296.2k-359.8k (-13.8% to +4.7%) and 64.5% of draws exceed 4%; q=10% and q=20% exceed 4% in 61.5% of draws; only q=50% stays inside 4% in every draw. The algebraic invariance is exact in expectation, but the inversion is ill-conditioned when p*mu is small (mu ~ sqrt(2(r-1))).

replacement_text.english: Each order is retained independently with probability p. Between two consecutive observed orders of a bicycle, missed orders are geometric, so the pair is adjacent in the true history with probability exactly p. Adjacency is observable through parking: with no missed order, the next trip starts where the previous ended. Exact cell matching recovers only same-cell returns; about a third of true adjacent returns cross a boundary. The 12.8% exact-match rate is therefore a lower bound. Widening to 160 m gives 17.7% and to 250 m 20.0%; net of the 2.3% false-match rate measured on definitely-moved pairs, the implied retention is 18% (range 13-20%). Pending the main-value decision, p=0.128 is retained for scaling, so every absolute count is an upper estimate by roughly 40%; ratios are unaffected, and the fleet estimate is algebraically invariant, but the occupancy estimator is biased down by a few percent (2.8% at half the sample).

reasons.8: no optimisation or ODE is solved in T002; the only boundaries are p in (0,1), distance thresholds inclusive, and the observed union as a lower bound, all checked in 2-4.
reasons.7: data/ excluding data/runs has 0 changed, 0 added, 0 removed against the T001 start fingerprint.

notes: The three lead ratios are reproduced exactly only under definition A; the same-user and same-day variants give much higher rates, so the definition must be stated with the number.
The exact-match rate is biased DOWN, not up: a_0=0.685 means 31.5% of true adjacent returns cross a geohash boundary; false matches on moved pairs are only 0.53% at d=0.
The paper's 'within 4%' resampling claim holds for its seed but not in distribution; see resample.verdict. This affects the sentence at sec9:35-37 and sec3:93-94, not the algebra.
Absolute quantities at p=0.18 shrink by 28.9% (factor 0.711); the classification CSV gives each value.
Untested branches: (i) p varying by hour/zone; (ii) order retention correlated with trip length; (iii) geohash jitter calibrated from start_lat_err rather than the placebo null.
